note: Judgements from sources and our own adapter work on the date shown, not benchmarks. A tool marked not run was scored from its description only, and a source marked not fetched was not read.

groups.job: Accounting system (where approved bills become draft entries and invoices are read from)

recommendation.beginner: QuickBooks Online if the client already uses it, because it is the most common choice for a small business and Booklantern's adapter was tested against a stand in for it. If they have no system yet, start with the CSV adapter and decide later.
recommendation.implementer: Use whatever the client already keeps their books in. QuickBooks is the tested path. Xero and Akaunting adapters are written from documentation and need a test against the client's own sandbox before you rely on them.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: Akaunting is open source and you can host it yourself, which removes the subscription but adds a server and your time. Check the current price pages of each tool yourself before you decide.
recommendation.open_source_when: Open source is the right call when a client wants their books on their own server or will not pay a subscription and someone can keep the server updated. It is the wrong call when the client's accountant already works inside QuickBooks or Xero.

groups.job: Payment links on reminders (a link a customer can use to pay an invoice)

recommendation.beginner: Stripe payment links, because the client may already have a Stripe account and the adapter only creates links. It never captures a payment or moves money.
recommendation.implementer: Keep draft mode on until the client has seen a placeholder link in a reminder. Test with Stripe test keys before any live key.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: Stripe charges a fee when a customer pays. Read the current pricing page for the client's country before you promise anything.
recommendation.open_source_when: No open source payment processor is scored here. Self hosted tools still need a bank or card network behind them.

tools.name: Stripe payment links
tools.supported_in_booklantern: Adapter tested against a stand in server

fit.evidence: The create endpoint and its fields were read on the date shown. The adapter sends an idempotency key so a retry cannot make two links.

setup.evidence: An account and a restricted key are needed. Not run, so judgement.

reliability.evidence: Hosted by the vendor and a mature service. No outage data was checked.

cost.evidence: Fees apply when a customer pays; no price was fetched.

data.evidence: Customer payment data sits with the vendor. Booklantern stores only the link.

integration.evidence: Create link only. Webhooks for paid status are not used, a bank statement line closes the invoice instead.

groups.job: Where bills arrive (a mailbox Booklantern reads)

recommendation.beginner: A dedicated mailbox on Gmail with an app password, because most small businesses have one. Use a mailbox just for bills.
recommendation.implementer: Create a separate mailbox such as bills at the client's domain and point suppliers at it. The reader only looks at unread mail and marks it read once its bills are saved. Mail with no bill in it stays unread. Set REPLY_TO to another mailbox a person reads.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: Any mail host that offers IMAP works and the reader adds no cost of its own.
recommendation.open_source_when: A self hosted mail server is the right call only if the client already runs one. Do not start one for this.

tools.name: Gmail over IMAP
tools.supported_in_booklantern: Adapter tested against a mock IMAP server

fit.evidence: Reads unread mail, keeps only PDF, PNG and JPEG attachments and ignores the rest. Gmail specific settings were not read.

setup.evidence: Needs two step sign in and an app password. Google can change that rule, so check it before you promise it.

reliability.evidence: A mature service, but app passwords can be withdrawn by Google.

cost.evidence: Works with a normal mailbox. No price checked.

integration.evidence: Tested against a local mock server for unread, attachments, marking seen after the bills are saved, and leaving mail without a bill unread.

data.evidence: Depends on where the host is.

integration.evidence: Same tests as the Gmail case, no host specific checks.

groups.job: The reader that turns a bill document into fields

recommendation.beginner: Use the offline reader for the demo. For real bills turn on the live reader with an Anthropic key, and keep a person approving every bill.
recommendation.implementer: The live reader path is written and UNVERIFIED. Run the held out set in docs/EXTRACTION-EVAL.md against it before a client sees it, and save the first run untouched.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: Pay per bill only on the bills you read. The offline reader costs nothing but cannot read pictures.
recommendation.open_source_when: Open source OCR is the right call when bills must not leave the client's machine. Expect more setup and lower accuracy on odd layouts.

recommendation.beginner: Vercel for the web app plus Railway for the API and worker, because there are no servers to look after.
recommendation.implementer: Hetzner with Docker Compose gives one bill and the most control, and you handle updates and backups. Use Vercel plus Hetzner when you want the web side managed.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: A small Hetzner server is usually the cheapest way to run the API and database. Read each price page yourself on the day you decide.
recommendation.open_source_when: Self hosting on a plain server is right when the client wants the data in their own region or you already run servers. It is not right for a first project with no one to do updates.
